term: attitude independence in the explanation-order test
definition: Practice indexes differing acceptance patterns. Beings, due goods and possessed goods are held literally fixed; the evil-exists sentence is true under each practice. This is an adopted test of independence from variation in acceptance with fixed facts, not a metaphysical possible-world claim or a definition of robust truth.
note: A deliberately limited fixture condition for issue #191. A fuller philosophical account would require a sourced account of which counterfactual changes preserve moral facts.
